heard: Astronauts don't float in space because gravity is gone. At the altitude of the International Space Station, Earth's gravity is roughly 90 percent as strong as it is at the surface. So why does the crew experience total weightlessness? The answer is that they and their spacecraft are in a continuous state of free fall. The station moves sideways so fast that as it falls toward the planet, the surface curves away beneath it. This means the crew completes one full orbit around Earth, approximately every 90 minutes. Because everything falls together, there is no floor pushing back, proving astronauts don't float because gravity is gone.
